**Draft text — progress update for Professor Reyes**

Subject: Decoherence pathways manuscript — progress update

Dear Professor Reyes,

- **Introduction.** A unified treatment framing has been drafted and corrected to accurately reflect the scope of the classification — "decoherence resolves into three identifiable pathways" rather than a claim of exhaustiveness. The opening paragraphs establish the gap in the literature and position our contribution relative to the stabilizer-formalism program.

- **Section 2 (model and measurement architecture).** The model assumptions (A1)–(A4), the Born-Markov master equation, and the dephasing-rate expression (Eq. 9) are in place. This section was sent to you on October 6 and is awaiting your written comments, particularly on the severity of the rates in Eq. (9) and the bridge paragraph into Section 3.

- **Section 3 (pathway classification and results).** A working draft containing the three-pathway classification (P1–P3), the crossover calculation, and the signature discriminability discussion was sent to you on October 7. The rate numbers in Section 3.2 are noted as stale and will be refreshed before submission. Revision notes from your feedback have been applied.

**Journal target.** Physical Review Letters. The decision was based on the compactness of the pathway classification and the broad-interest hook of the crossover-depth prediction.

**Citation progress.** Two key candidate citations have been evaluated against the manuscript's citation rule and found to satisfy it: Reyes 2024 (PRB 110, 195433) for the conditioned-readout result, and Okonkwo 2024 (PRL 132, 146601) for the intrinsic-visibility bound. The citation insertion for the latter in Section 2.3 remains pending and will be applied in the next draft session.

**Next steps.** Your written comments on Sections 2 and 3 will be processed during the follow-up slot on Thursday October 15 (09:30–11:00). Thereafter the outstanding clerical items — the trace-out citation decision, the stabilizer-contrast paragraph citations, and the conversion of the Braithwaite poisoning entry — will be resolved, and the cover letter drafted ahead of submission.

Please let me know if any further detail would be useful.

Best regards,
